tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent/triggers ('why is my AWS Config bill so high', 'reduce Config costs'), lists explicit trigger contexts beyond direct domain naming, and while it is longer than a couple sentences, it remains a single cohesive paragraph appropriately scoped to the skill's breadth without excessive implementation detail in the trigger-listing portion.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize AWS Config spend, or reports an unexpected AWS Config cost or configuration-item increase. Activate on requests like "why is my AWS Config bill so high"...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is focused on domain-specific procedures and facts (billing model essentials, workflow steps, severity definitions, gotchas) rather than general concepts the agent would already know. It doesn't explain what AWS Config is or general API concepts.
tests.evidence: Configuration items (CIs) are the dominant cost driver — billed per CI recorded.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference material (billing charge tables, API call details, opportunity check definitions) is moved to references/ files and only summarized briefly in the body. No large blocks of reference data or detailed conditional-branch data are embedded in the body itself.
tests.evidence: For the full charge table, per-mode pricing, and the high-churn reasoning the checks rely on, load [references/billing-model.md](references/billing-model.md)

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three reference files (billing-model.md, data-collection.md, opportunities.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies a clear condition for when to load it (e.g., deciding continuous vs daily, collecting API data, analyzing opportunities).
tests.evidence: load [references/billing-model.md](references/billing-model.md) when you need to decide whether continuous or daily is cheaper for a resource type, or to explain a charge.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root in the format references/filename.md.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/compliance-sensitive operations (read-only boundaries, conformance-pack overlap, compliance tradeoffs) are given exact prescriptive instructions, while flexible analysis steps (scope selection, signal collection) allow reasoning and explain why, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: Never recommend dropping recording below the organization's audit requirements.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When multiple signal sources are mentioned for cost/volume collection, a clear preferred default and fallback order is given rather than a flat list of equal options.
tests.evidence: Prefer Cost Explorer as the dollar signal, use Athena (or `GetDiscoveredResourceCounts` as an approximate fallback) for CI-driver attribution

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (scope identification, inventory, cost signal collection, opportunity analysis, validation, reporting) applicable to any Config cost review, not a one-off declarative task.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Identify target scope. Ask the user which accounts and Regions to review...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Known Quirks' section with concrete, non-obvious environment-specific facts (e.g., Control Tower recorder resets, GetDiscoveredResourceCounts limitations, conformance-pack overlap intent).
tests.evidence: In Control Tower / Organizations environments, recorder settings may be centrally managed and reset on account provisioning...

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides an explicit output template in assets/report-template.md referenced from Step 6, satisfying the need for structured report output.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output template is embedded inline in the body; the report template lives entirely in assets/report-template.md and is only referenced.
tests.evidence: Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file report-template.md is linked in Step 6 of the workflow.
tests.evidence: [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies exactly when to load it — during Step 6 report generation.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root in correct format.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The workflow is presented as an ordered checklist using '- [ ] Step N:' format exactly as required, with dependent sequential steps.
tests.evidence: - [ ] **Step 1: Identify target scope.** ... - [ ] **Step 2: Inventory the Config setup.**

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 5 explicitly instructs the agent to self-check its findings for accuracy, traceability of savings estimates, compliance tradeoffs, and absence of mutation calls before presenting the report.
tests.evidence: Step 5: Validate findings. Before writing the report, self-check the findings: confirm each estimated saving traces to a cited signal... Drop or re-label any finding that fails these checks.
